items.title: Vibe physics: The AI grad student
items.summary: A Harvard physicist guided Claude Opus 4.5 through a full quantum chromodynamics research project in two weeks.

items.title: Claude-shaped science
items.summary: Matthew Schwartz describes what happened when he stopped fighting Claude and allowed Claude to find “Claude-shaped” problems. This led him to build BootLoops, a toolkit for exact calculations in quantitative science, which he has been applying across scientific fields alongside experts.

items.title: Claude accelerates protein design and analytical chemistry
items.summary: Two results show how Claude helps life sciences researchers speed up their work: designing protein binders from scratch and analyzing NMR and LC-MS data to speed chemical analysis.

items.title: Enabling independent research on how people use Claude
items.summary: Earlier this year, we ran a pilot giving external researchers access to aggregate, real-world Claude usage data. Three research groups designed their own studies for Anthropic Insights, our privacy-preserving analysis tool. In this post, we share high-level results from those studies and what we learned running this pilot.

items.title: Scaling Managed Agents with stable interfaces
items.summary: Harnesses encode assumptions that go stale as models improve. See how Managed Agents is built around interfaces that stay stable as harnesses change.

items.title: Discovering and exploiting vulnerabilities in critical, real-world software with Claude
items.summary: Over the past few months, we’ve used an unreleased, internal research model to find critical vulnerabilities in some of the world’s most widely used software, such as browsers and operating systems. In this post, we share details of five attack chains, which led to remote code execution and other critical impacts with little to no user interaction.
